overview: This bill, called the Breaking the Gridlock Act, would extend for three more years the larger "premium tax credits" that help people pay for health insurance bought through the Affordable Care Act marketplaces, such as HealthCare.gov. These enhanced credits, which lower monthly premiums, expired at the end of 2025; the bill would bring them back for tax years 2026 through 2028. It would also keep the rule that lets people earning more than four times the federal poverty line qualify for help, rather than cutting them off. The House passed it on January 8, 2026, and as of February 10, 2026, it was on the Senate's calendar awaiting possible action.
for: Supporters say restoring the larger credits keeps health coverage affordable for millions of people who saw their premiums jump when the enhanced help expired.
against: Critics say extending the credits adds substantial federal cost and sends subsidies to higher-income households, without addressing the underlying cost of health insurance.
